strings: The Gaping Chasm is a sprawling silithid hive carved deep into the sands of southeastern Tanaris. Infested by aggressive insectoid horrors of the Hazzali brood, it serves as a grim warning of the growing silithid menace spreading beyond the western deserts.

Breaking the rolling expanses of Tanaris, the Gaping Chasm plunges down into a teeming subterranean warren of tunnels, resinous mounds, and twitching carapaces. This hive belongs to the Hazzali, an aggressive brood of silithid that have burrowed beneath the desert wastes. Between subterranean stingers, swarmers, and hulking sandreavers, any travelers or treasure-hunters foolish enough to descend into the chasm quickly find themselves hunted as prey or preserved in sticky cocoons.

The expanding hive caught the attention of Gadgetzan's enterprising minds, prompting Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser to dispatch his junior surveyor, Scrimshank, into the pit to map and measure the geological shifts caused by the insect tunnels. Unsurprisingly, the expedition ended in disaster. Scrimshank met a grim end amidst the chittering broods, leaving behind scattered gear and measuring instruments that caution anyone against underestimating the silithid threat.
What creatures dwell inside the Gaping Chasm?

The chasm is infested entirely by the Hazzali silithid. The hive includes numerous castes of the insectoid species, such as worker drones, winged stingers, overwhelming swarms, and massive, chitin-plated sandreavers.

Garren's Haunt is an abandoned farmstead nestled in northern Tirisfal Glades. Once a prosperous human homestead, the farm fell to ruin when the Scourge wiped out the Garren family, leaving the overgrown grounds overrun by feral Rot Hide gnolls.

Before the Third War, this farmstead supported a family and produced bountiful harvests under the Kingdom of Lordaeron. When the Plague of Undeath swept across the countryside, the Scourge descended upon the farm and slaughtered Garren and his kin. Today, the fields lie gray and withered, the farmhouse and barn decaying under the perpetual gloom of Tirisfal.

Rather than standard Scourge patrols, Garren's Haunt has been claimed by the Rot Hide gnolls—a pack of undead-tainted scavengers led by the vicious Maggot Eye. These scavengers aggressively defend their reclaimed territory, picking clean whatever remains of the farm and savaging any travelers or Forsaken patrols passing along northern Tirisfal.

The Garrison Armory is an Alliance mining operation carved into the hills southwest of Nethergarde Keep in the Blasted Lands. Miners and engineers work the underground veins to harvest valuable minerals, sustaining the lonely fortress and shipping raw wealth back to Stormwind. It forms a crucial industrial lifeline in an otherwise blasted, barren wilderness.
A Lifeline in the Red Wastes

Maintaining a permanent military garrison in the arid wastes of the Blasted Lands requires constant supply, and Nethergarde Keep cannot rely purely on long supply trains from Stormwind. The Garrison Armory serves as the keep's primary industrial excavation. Nethergarde miners, overseen by foremen and assisted by engineers, work these subterranean shafts to pull valuable minerals from the earth. The ore extracted here is utilized directly by Nethergarde's smiths and fortifications or hauled back to the capital in exchange for the foodstuffs, tools, and provisions the fortress needs to maintain its vigil over the Dark Portal.

Because the armory sits away from the main walls of Nethergarde Keep, the excavation remains exposed to the harsh perils of the red desert. Trolls, ogres, and wild beasts prowl the surrounding crags, while agents of the Horde keep a close eye on Nethergarde's mining output. The workforce within the tunnels operates under armed guard, knowing that any disruption to the armory directly threatens Nethergarde's ability to maintain its watch over the blasted frontier.

The Garrison Armory is an Alliance mining complex operated by Nethergarde Keep. Workers extract metal and minerals underground to maintain the fortress and trade back to Stormwind for essential food and equipment.

The Gates of Ironforge serve as the monumental main entrance leading travelers from the snowy mountain vales of Dun Morogh into the dwarven capital. Carved directly into the sheer stone face of the mountain, they are guarded inside by a colossal statue of High King Modimus Anvilmar.

Approached by climbing the winding, fortified ramp ascending from central Dun Morogh, the Gates of Ironforge present an imposing facade visible across much of the snowy lowlands. Beyond the massive portal, visitors enter the city proper, greeted immediately by an enormous stone statue honoring High King Modimus Anvilmar—the legendary ruler who united the dwarven clans before the War of the Three Hammers. Passing through these gates leads directly into the bustling commercial district of the Commons.

The Gates of Orgrimmar form the imposing southern threshold of the Horde capital, carved directly into the red rock of northern Durotar. Flanked by heavy timber and iron battlements, this grand entryway connects the arid wastes outside to the busy commons of the Valley of Strength. It stands as a physical declaration of orcish endurance and martial strength.

Framed by towering wooden palisades, massive iron spikes, and fortified watchtowers, the main gate guards the primary chasm cutting into the mountains sheltering Orgrimmar. For travelers approaching from Razor Hill and the scrublands of Durotar, the entrance serves as both a welcoming monument and a stark deterrent to any who would threaten the new Horde. Heavily armed Orgrimmar Grunts and Darkspear Headhunters patrol the approach, keeping vigilant watch over all traffic entering the city.

Passing beneath the shadowed arch of the gates leads directly into the Valley of Strength, the civic and martial heart of Orgrimmar. The gate tunnel acts as an acoustic and tactical bottleneck, funneling envoys, merchants, and warriors past watchful sentries. It represents the realization of Warchief Thrall's dream: a secure sanctuary carved from the harsh desert where the disparate peoples of the Horde can walk united without fear.

Gelkis Village is the primary stronghold of the earth-aligned Gelkis centaur clan in southwestern Desolace. Built around a rugged ravine connected by wooden spans and cliffside paths, the settlement guards the southern route toward Feralas. Its vantage directly overlooks the main north-south road, making it a perilous crossing for any traveler who has not earned the clan's favor.

Gelkis Village sits in a deep, craggy gorge framed by precarious bluffs and rope bridges. Unlike the nomadic raiders of the Barrens, the Gelkis have fortified their ancestral grounds into a permanent settlement, complete with outposts spreading toward the border of Feralas. The heart of the clan's leadership lies within Bolgan's Hole, a cavern carved into the southern cliff face where Khan Shaka oversees his warriors. Travelers trekking south through Desolace must either cut a bloody path through the gorge or tread carefully, as the Gelkis view uninvited wanderers as fair game in their eternal war against their rival centaur brethren.

The settlement belongs to the Gelkis clan, one of the five warring centaur tribes native to Desolace. They are staunch earth-worshipers ruled by Khan Shaka, who resides deep in the cliffside cave known as Bolgan's Hole.

Ghost Walker Post is a modest tauren settlement situated in the heart of Desolace right beside the ancient Kodo Graveyard. Far more exposed to regional dangers than Shadowprey Village on the western coast, it serves as a frontline Horde staging ground against centaur clans and the Burning Blade.

Perched on the dusty flats of central Desolace, Ghost Walker Post provides the Horde with an austere foothold in a hostile territory. Unlike the sheltered coastal fishing haven of Shadowprey Village, this post directly faces roaming centaur marauders and demon-worshiping cultists of the Burning Blade. Facilities are spartan, offering only the bare essentials for travelers, with no inn or flight master in sight. Despite the harsh conditions, a garrison of tauren and an orcish detachment sent by Warchief Thrall keep vigilant watch over the badlands.

Led by the tauren shaman Gurda Wildmane, the spiritual heart of the outpost is closely entwined with the neighboring Kodo Graveyard. Shamans stationed here tend to the dying beasts that wander in to perish, helping ease them into the next life and communing with their lingering spirits. Between spiritual communion and constant military readiness, the defenders of the post honor the ancient bond between the tauren and the mighty kodo amid the ashes of Desolace.

Though remote, the shoreline shares in Darkshore's characteristic gloom, washed by cold waters and framed by ancient coastal pines.

Gnomeregan was the magnificent subterranean capital of the gnomish race, renowned across Azeroth for its mechanical brilliance and technological marvels. Today, it stands as a radioactive tomb, overrun by subterranean troggs, haywire defense automatons, and deranged leper gnomes after a desperate defense ended in catastrophe.

Carved into the snowy crags of western Dun Morogh, Gnomeregan was built with the aid of the Ironforge dwarves centuries ago. Inside, massive steam-driven gears, intricate copper piping, and cavernous assembly halls formed the intellectual and industrial beating heart of gnomekind. It was from these subterranean halls that gnomish designs, flying machines, and complex armaments supplied the Alliance throughout the Second War, standing firm even when besieged by Orgrim Doomhammer's Horde.
The Fall and the Poisoned Halls

During the Third War, a subterranean surge of troggs erupted from deep beneath the earth, breaching the city's lowest chambers. Unwilling to divert Alliance armies from the slaughter in Lordaeron, High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque attempted to handle the crisis alone. On the advice of his chief engineer, Sicco Thermaplugg, Mekkatorque ordered radioactive gas vented through the lower chambers to wipe out the brutes. The plan backfired horrifyingly: the gas empowered many troggs while killing nearly eighty percent of the gnomish populace. Those exposed who did not perish mutated into twisted leper gnomes, while Thermaplugg seized rule over the poisoned ruins.

The desperate gambit was intended to eradicate the beasts, but instead it slaughtered thousands of gnomes, mutated the survivors into leper gnomes, and left the city permanently irradiated.

Go'Shek Farm is an agricultural outpost in the eastern Arathi Highlands, occupied by the Horde and guarded by orcs from Hammerfall. Behind its mundane rural facade, Forsaken apothecaries conduct secretive alchemical experiments far from prying eyes.
A Horde Outpost in the East

Once a human farmstead held by Second War veterans, Go'Shek Farm fell into Horde hands following the chaos of the Third War. Positioned south of Hammerfall and just north of the hostile Witherbark troll territory, the farmstead nominally serves as a vital supply and staging hub for the orcish settlement. Hammerfall Grunts patrol the fields and stables, securing food and livestock to sustain the Horde's embattled foothold in the Arathi Highlands.

Beneath the routine work of tilling soil and tending beasts lies a darker purpose. The Royal Apothecary Society has established a quiet presence at the farmstead, led by figures such as Apothecary Jorell. Couriers slip between Go'Shek Farm and Tarren Mill, ferrying notes, reagents, and research into early variants of the Forsaken's new plague. The Alliance has taken notice, dispatching scouts to intercept these messengers and uncover the nature of the poison brewing in the Arathi soil.

Centered around a massive smelting cauldron, the chamber fell into chaos when the experimental harvest golems housed within abruptly came to life.

Carved into the subterranean depths of Moonbrook, the Goblin Foundry provided the Defias Brotherhood with the heavy manufacturing power required to fuel their uprising. Utilizing vast smelters, iron ramps, and goblin engineering expertise, the workshop mass-produced mechanical armaments. Among their most ambitious endeavors was the construction of the Foe Reaper 5000, an upgraded iteration of Westfall's familiar automated reapers.

Goblin ingenuity notoriously borders on catastrophe, and the foundry's crowning achievement proved to be its undoing. Gol'Bolar Quarry is a dwarven excavation site carved into the snowy hills of southeastern Dun Morogh. Rich in stone and ore, the bustling mining operation has ground to a halt after being overrun by vicious troggs surging from the depths.

Situated southeast of Kharanos, Gol'Bolar Quarry was established by Ironforge dwarves to extract vital stone and mineral wealth from the mountains. However, deep excavation work uncovered underground warrens, unleashing a horde of hostile troggs that quickly drove out the miners.
